prompts.Front:
Use case: sketch-to-render. Create one premium photorealistic architectural elevation of JESB LOT7 R09. Input image 1 is the authoritative geometry and material placement source. Preserve exact camera elevation projection, building silhouette, roof forms, all opening positions and sizes, grids, grouped headers, sills, trims, stair geometry, railings and grade. No architectural redesign. Render existing materials only: Mission Brown asphalt shingles on main roofs; dark brown bronze standing seam METAL on accent roofs (the patterned shiny brown source texture represents standing seam metal, not tiles); Magnolia pale warm cream brick with subtle varied tones and fine mortar, Cobble Stone warm pale greige lap siding, white decorative panels/window frames/trims/soffits/fascia; brown entry and garage doors, light beige cast-stone headers, existing black iron rails. Preserve exact material boundaries. Premium Corona-style architectural visualization finish with convincing fine surface texture, restrained roughness, soft daylight, gentle dimensional shadows, natural exposure, neutral whites, no oversaturation, no excessive contrast. Realistic glazing reflecting only sky and grass with subtle dark interior depth; no invented furniture, trees or vegetation in reflections. Surroundings ONLY short natural grass, existing hardscape and lightly clouded blue sky. Preserve slopes and existing driveway footprint; no trees, shrubs, cars, people, planting beds, new paths or props. Straight verticals and source orthographic elevation, full building uncropped, no perspective conversion. Very high detail at highest available native output resolution, landscape. No drawing outlines, annotations, text, watermark, blur, bloom or oversharpening.
FRONT / WEST elevation. Preserve stepped foreground slope, overlapping front gables, small upper gable window, white lower gable face and white decorative panels, entry sidelights and right-side covered terrace. Image 2 is depth/site reference ONLY; do not adopt its camera. Maintain source elevation architecture.
